title: Detection of RNA-DNA hybrids by immunostaining in meiotic nuclei of Saccharomyces cerevisiae
protocol: Patch cells from glycerol storage at -80°C onto YPG plates and incubate at 30°C overnight (∼14–16 h).
Streak yeast cells onto YPD plates and incubate at 30°C for 2–3 days (54–56 h) to obtain single colonies.
Inoculate a whole colony into 4 mL YPD liquid medium in a test tube.
Grow the culture at 30°C for 24 h on a roller.
Set up three cultures for each strain.
Pick two good YPD cultures for each strain.
Dilute each one into 150 mL SPS II medium in a 2 L flask using a 1/500 dilution for the WT strain (300 μL).
Dilute each one into 150 mL SPS II medium in a 2 L flask using a 1/50 dilution for the rnh1Δrnh201Δhpr1Δ mutant (3 mL).
Incubate at 30°C for approximately 16 hours in a shaker with 200 rpm.
Select one better culture to prepare the meiosis culture for each strain.
Measure the optical density (OD600) of the undiluted culture using a spectrophotometer.
Use SPS II medium as a blank control during OD measurement.
Assess the percentage of G1/G0 cells by DAPI staining.
Evaluate the presence of vegetative S-phase and mitosis cells via DAPI staining.
Ensure the percentage of cells in vegetative S-phase and mitosis is less than 10%.
Check for premature entry into meiosis by absence of large buds with DAPI at or stretched across the neck.
Examine cell morphology to identify 4–8 daughter and mother cells at similar size beaded together.
Determine a well-synchronized culture based on the presence of numerous beaded cells.
Centrifuge cells in 175 mL centrifuge bottles at 1,800 × g for 2 min at 25°C.
Resuspend cells with 150 mL prewarmed SPM.
Repeat steps b and c as necessary.
Transfer each resuspended culture into one 2 L flask.
Incubate cultures in a shaker incubator at 30°C, ∼200 rpm.
Record the time as 0 h.
Prewarm all media used for step from 5°C to 30°C in an incubator before use.
Collect 10 mL of meiotic culture every hour during 0–8 h in SPM.
Pellet cells at 1,000 × g for 2 min at 25°C using a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells with 2.5 mL 200 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.5).
Add 50 μL of 1 M DTT to the cell suspension and mix well.
Let stand at 25°C for 2 min.
Pellet cells at 1,000 × g for 2 min at 25°C.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend with 2.5 mL ZK buffer.
Add 5 μL zymolyase 100T solution and mix well.
Incubate at 30°C on a roller for ∼25 min, resuspend cells by inverting tubes every 5–10 min during incubation.
Check progress by placing ∼1 μL of mixture into a large drop of water on a slide and observe under a light microscope.
If >90% of cells burst within 1 min, the spheroplasts are ready, then put the samples on ice to stop the reaction.
Pellet cells at 800 × g for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend in 5 mL cold MES wash buffer.
Pellet cells at 800 × g for 2 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in a suitable volume of MES wash buffer (can just barely see through suspension if you lift it up against the light).
Put 20 μL cells on a slide.
Add 40 μL 3% paraformaldehyde with 3.4% sucrose to cells, then quickly add 80 μL 1% lipsol.
Mix well with swirling.
Check under a microscope, when ∼90% of cells explode (usually within 1 min).
Then add 80 μL 3% paraformaldehyde with 3.4% sucrose to the mixture and mix.
Spread with a clean glass pipet.
Dry in air.
Dip slides vertically in 0.2% photoflo for 30 s.
Allow to dry.
Dip in 1× TBS in a horizontal Coplin jar for 15 min.
Drain the liquid thoroughly but do not dry it.
Place the slides horizontally in a moist chamber.
Add 200 μL of 1× TBS with 1% BSA to each slide, cover with a coverslip, and incubate for 10 minutes at 25°C.
Drain as above.
Dilute the S9.6 antibody using 1× TBS with 1% BSA (1:1,000 dilution).
Apply 200 μL of diluted antibody solution to each slide.
Cover with a coverslip and incubate overnight (∼8–10 hours) at 4°C in a moist chamber.
Shake the slide gently to remove the coverslip.
Apply approximately 700 μL of 1× TBS to cover the slide and incubate for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Drain.
Repeat steps as above twice more.
Add 200 μL of diluted secondary antibody (1:1,000 donkey anti-mouse Alexa 488 in 1× TBS with 1% BSA) to each slide under subdued light.
Cover with a coverslip and incubate for 1–3 hours at 25°C in a moist chamber in the dark.
Remove coverslip and wash with 1× TBS as before.
Dry in the dark.
Put one drop of antifade solution containing DAPI on each slide.
Cover with a 24 × 50 mm coverslip, seal with clear nail polish.
Store at -20°C in a 100-slide storage box for up to two months or store indefinitely at -80°C.
Dip the slide into 0.2% photoflo for 30 s.
Air dry the slide.
If necessary, test the specificity of S9.6 antibody using RNase H treated sample as negative control.
Dilute RNase H enzymes in 1× RNase H buffer at a ratio of 1:200.
Add 200 μL diluted RNase H enzymes to each slide.
Cover with coverslip and incubate in moist chamber for 2–3 h at 37°C.
Remove the coverslip after incubation.
Wash the slide in TBS as before.
If necessary, use RNase A solution to minimize rRNA interference.
Dilute RNase A (10 mg/mL) with 300 mM NaCl solution to a concentration of 0.6 ng/μL.
Add 200 μL diluted RNase A to each slide.
Cover the slide with coverslip and incubate in moist chamber for 2–3 h at 37°C.
Remove the coverslip after incubation.
Wash the slide in TBS as before.
Perform S9.6 immunofluorescence staining according to steps 28–40.
Incubate samples for fluorescence microscopy.
Take images with a 100× 1.6 NA oil-immersion objective.
Capture images on two channels individually.
Observe the signal of DAPI.
Observe the signal of RNA-DNA hybrids.
